title: Streamlined enterprise intake & curation process for chat-to-tool workflows and structured responses
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Problem: Enterprise customers frequently request combinations of features (chat streaming + tool/function calling + structured outputs) as a single project. Current intake is fragmented: requests land across support, Sales, and solutions, which causes inconsistent prioritization, repeated discovery calls, and long time-to-first-prototype. Goal: define a repeatable intake and prioritization pipeline specifically for multi-signal Hosted API feature requests (chat streaming, tool/function calls, and structured outputs) that balances enterprise SLAs, security/compliance needs, and engineering cost/latency trade-offs. Outcome should reduce discovery cycles, accelerate pilot delivery, and produce clear gating criteria for Dedicated/Private offers.
customer_requests: Large customer wants streaming chat with server-side tool execution and JSON-structured outputs for compliance logs
FinReg customer requires function-calling with end-to-end audit trails and deterministic structured fields for downstream processing
SaaS platform requests canary rollout plan for streaming + tool-calls with per-tenant quotas and fallback model variants
triage_criteria: Revenue or ARR influence (enterprise contract size / leverage)
Technical coupling complexity (requires runtime changes: streaming + KV cache + tool-call orchestration)
Latency/SLO impact (tight p95 targets or synchronous flows)
Data residency or private deployment requirement
Ability to prototype using existing model variants and runtime (low/medium/high)
proposed_workflow: 1) Unified intake form (pre-filled by AE/CS) that captures use case, required SLOs, compliance constraints, desired structured schema, and example prompts. 2) Automated scoring: revenue, compliance urgency, technical risk, and prototype feasibility. 3) Weekly enterprise triage slot (PM + Eng tech lead + Solutions + Security) to convert scored requests into one of: 'Pilot', 'Research spike', 'Routed to Dedicated/Private', or 'Deferred'. 4) For 'Pilot' items: create a scoped PRD with a 4-week prototype plan, engineering tickets (ENG-xxx), and a design sketch for structured output schemas. 5) Run a 2-week pilot/canary with telemetry hooks (console dashboards) and success metrics. 6) Commit to rollout path: hosted GA, dedicated offering, or private deployment with migration checklist and docs.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form template published and available to AE/CS (Confluence link in links)
Automated scoring script implemented and integrated with intake (minimum 4 criteria)
Triage cadence booked and stakeholders assigned
Three pilot requests processed end-to-end using the workflow with timelines and outcome notes
Telemetry: pipeline captures time-to-prototype, conversion-to-pilot rate, and customer satisfaction post-pilot
Security checklist and data-residency gating included in PRD for any request that flags compliance
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Engineering capacity for combined runtime changes (streaming + tool orchestration). Mitigation: require feasibility spike and include ENG-7234 dependency for runtime scheduling improvements.
Risk: Over-indexing on low-value customizations. Mitigation: strict revenue/compliance scoring threshold before Pilot approval.
Risk: Unknown quality regressions from structured-output schema changes. Mitigation: tie every Pilot to an eval suite and automatic regression alerts in Redwood Optimize.
Risk: Security review bottleneck. Mitigation: pre-authorized security template for common request patterns and a fast-track intake for low-risk items.
Risk: Customer expects bespoke SLAs before technical validation. Mitigation: configurable pilot SLAs with explicit fallback policies and documented escalation path.
